root_cause.text: In `mptcp_recvmsg()`, when `MSG_PEEK` is used, skbs are not removed from the receive queue, causing `sk_wait_data()` to always see available data and never block, leading to a soft lockup when combined with `MSG_WAITALL`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "When receiving data with MSG_PEEK | MSG_WAITALL flags, the skb is not removed from the sk_receive_queue. This causes sk_wait_data() to always find available data and never perform actual waiting, leading to a soft lockup." The patch adds a `last` parameter to track the last peeked skb and passes it to `sk_wait_data()` so it can make informed waiting decisions. (See the diff changes in `__mptcp_recvmsg_mskq` and `mptcp_recvmsg`.)
